classification_scope: Research suitability. KEEP is not a redistribution approval. REPLACE recommends a new research role/source under a new ID; never retarget the existing ID.

revision_profiles.CPI_SA: Annual seasonal-factor recalculation can revise the preceding five years. Weights, sampling and methods evolve; preserve release vintages for historical information-set studies.
revision_profiles.CPI_NSA: No routine seasonal-factor revision; corrections and methodological/coverage changes remain possible. Do not describe the series as immutable.
revision_profiles.BEA_PRICES: Monthly estimates are revised with new inputs and annual/comprehensive NIPA updates. Chain weights, methods and reference years change; current history is not a release-time vintage.
revision_profiles.BEA_GDP: Advance, second and third quarterly estimates, followed by annual/comprehensive revisions. Annualized growth is already transformed; inspect vintage and reference-year changes.
revision_profiles.BEA_REAL: Monthly estimates and annual/comprehensive revisions; chain-linking and rebasing affect reported levels. Chained-dollar components are generally not additive outside the reference period.
revision_profiles.CPS: Seasonal revisions and population-control updates can change estimates or create breaks; historical treatment differs across levels and rates. Survey redesigns require source notes and vintages.
revision_profiles.CES: Initial estimates normally receive two monthly revisions; annual employment benchmarking, seasonal factors and methodological updates revise history. Changes in job mix matter for average earnings.
revision_profiles.JOLTS: Preliminary estimates receive revisions and annual benchmarking/seasonal updates. Scope is surveyed vacancies, not all internet advertisements.
revision_profiles.CLAIMS: Recent weeks can be revised; seasonal factors and estimation methods are updated. Pandemic distortions and reporting backlogs make a single weekly change noisy.
revision_profiles.H15: Correction-prone financial observations rather than macro survey vintages. Missing business-day quotes must remain missing; yields are fitted constant-maturity estimates, not tradable bond returns.
revision_profiles.EFFR_MONTH: Official monthly aggregation of daily effective rates. Daily methodology changed from brokered volume-weighted mean to FR 2420 transaction-based volume-weighted median on 2016-03-01; monthly figures include calendar days.
revision_profiles.STL_SPREAD: Derived from Treasury yield inputs; corrections and input-method/source changes propagate. FRED notes a Treasury input-source change in June 2019 for breakevens. Negative spreads/real yields are legitimate.
revision_profiles.CENSUS_SALES: Advance estimates are revised as fuller monthly information and annual benchmark inputs arrive; historical corrections and seasonal/trading-day factors can change the full path.
revision_profiles.CENSUS_HOUSING: Survey/administrative estimates receive monthly and annual seasonal revisions. Geographic coverage, authorizations, starts and completions are different populations/stages.
revision_profiles.G17: Recent monthly estimates, annual benchmarks, seasonal factors, industry weights and methods are revised. Rebased index levels are not tonnes or construction output.
revision_profiles.PMMS: Weekly estimates and corrections; major shift from the prior survey to application-based data on 2022-11-17. Historical publication weekdays differ; do not force Thursday labels backward.
revision_profiles.MICHIGAN: Preliminary/final survey readings differ; FRED delivery is delayed one month. Early pre-1978 history is sparse. Telephone-to-web transition April-July 2024 introduces method effects.
revision_profiles.ICE_OAS: Constituents rebalance and pricing/OAS models can change; historical corrections are possible. Current FRED access is a rolling three-year window from April 2026, not the index's full economic history.
revision_profiles.YAHOO_INDEX: Secondary-vendor corrections and backcasts are not a versioned original index archive. Price indexes exclude dividends; historical constituent/basket changes require original methodology.
revision_profiles.YAHOO_FUTURES: Per-bar contract selection, roll date, adjustment method and close/settlement identity are not established by the current adapter. Current history is not a frozen contract-level audit trail.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUSR0000SA0; FRED CPIAUCSL
datasets.suitable: Seasonally adjusted short-run consumer-price momentum and inflation-cycle comparisons.
datasets.unsuitable: Official NSA annual headline, individual household cost of living, policy announcement timing or point-in-time trading backtests using revised history.
datasets.continuity: Urban-consumer coverage and basket weights evolve; an index level is not an inflation rate. Annual SA changes differ from the official NSA headline.
datasets.alternatives: Existing cpi_nsa for official annual CPI; PCEPI for broader consumption prices; BLS release vintages for announcement studies.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUSR0000SA0L1E; FRED CPILFESL
datasets.suitable: Short-run consumer inflation excluding food and energy.
datasets.unsuitable: A complete household inflation burden, pure monetary-policy shock or the NSA core headline without choosing that separate series.
datasets.continuity: Excluding food/energy does not remove every transitory price movement; shelter lags and changing weights matter.
datasets.alternatives: Existing core_cpi_nsa and core_pce; Cleveland Fed median/trimmed-mean CPI under their own definitions and terms.

datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCERG; FRED PCEPI
datasets.producer: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.suitable: Broad consumption-price inflation and the price concept relevant to the Fed's longer-run inflation objective.
datasets.unsuitable: A substitute for CPI contract escalation, a fixed basket or a release-time policy information set without vintages.
datasets.continuity: Scope, third-party-paid consumption and chain weights differ from CPI; indexes cannot be spliced merely because both measure prices.
datasets.alternatives: Existing core_pce for food/energy exclusion and cpi_nsa for a different consumer-price scope; no wholesale replacement needed.

datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCCRG; FRED PCEPILFE
datasets.producer: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.suitable: Underlying consumption-price trends excluding food and energy, using the stated transformation.
datasets.unsuitable: An exact representation of all inflation faced by households or an unrevised policy-surprise series.
datasets.continuity: Chain weights and comprehensive revisions matter; core PCE and core CPI have different scopes and formulas.
datasets.alternatives: Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE as a separate robust-trend measure, with source-specific permission review.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS LNS14000000; FRED UNRATE
datasets.suitable: U-3 labour-market slack among the civilian labour force aged 16 and over.
datasets.unsuitable: The share of the entire population without a job, unique payroll job creation, or all underemployment.
datasets.continuity: Labour-force exits can reduce the rate without employment gains. Annual population controls and redesigns need review.
datasets.alternatives: U-6 (U6RATE), prime-age employment/population (LNS12300060), and existing participation/payrolls; each is a distinct concept.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CES0000000001; FRED PAYEMS
datasets.suitable: Establishment nonfarm payroll job levels and correctly scaled adjacent-month job changes.
datasets.unsuitable: Unique employed people, self-employment, a fixed unrevised jobs-announcement surprise or direct wage purchasing power.
datasets.continuity: Multiple jobholders may be counted more than once; employment benchmarks and business births/deaths affect revisions.
datasets.alternatives: CPS employment for people, QCEW for benchmarking, and original BLS release archives for announcement-time values.

datasets.original_identifier: BEA A191RL; FRED A191RL1Q225SBEA
datasets.suitable: Quarter-on-quarter annualized real US output growth.
datasets.unsuitable: A GDP level, ordinary quarterly percent change, year-on-year growth or a monthly activity observation.
datasets.continuity: Already annualized: do not apply another percentage-change transform or sum rates as though they were dollars.
datasets.alternatives: GDPC1 real GDP level for consistent YoY/level questions; final sales and GDI for complementary output evidence.

datasets.original_identifier: Board H.15 effective funds monthly; FRED FEDFUNDS
datasets.producer: Federal Reserve Board; underlying daily effective rates administered by New York Fed
datasets.suitable: Monthly overnight funding conditions and slow-moving policy-regime context.
datasets.unsuitable: Identifying first hike/cut announcement dates, target rates, daily event returns or monetary-policy surprises.
datasets.continuity: Averages mix before/after a decision and calendar-day weights. The 2016 calculation break is distinct from target-regime changes.
datasets.alternatives: Official FOMC statements/events; DFEDTAR and DFEDTARL/U for target states; DFF or NY Fed EFFR for daily implementation.

datasets.original_identifier: S&P DJI S&P 500 price index; secondary Yahoo ^GSPC
datasets.producer: S&P Dow Jones Indices; Yahoo redistributor
datasets.suitable: Qualified US large-cap price-index context after feed validation and permission clearance.
datasets.unsuitable: Dividend-inclusive investor performance, a tradable security or an unqualified pre-launch/live-constituent history.
datasets.continuity: Modern 500-stock index launched in 1957; earlier vendor history is a predecessor/backcast question. Yahoo firstTradeDate does not prove uniform construction.
datasets.alternatives: Licensed original S&P price and total-return series; a separately identified SPY total-return proxy only with dividends, fees, tracking and its 1993 inception disclosed.

datasets.original_identifier: COMEX GC underlying contract; vendor Yahoo GC=F continuation
datasets.producer: COMEX/CME contract market; vendor continuation construction not verified
datasets.suitable: Clearly qualified futures-price exploration, pending contract-map, close-time and rights validation.
datasets.unsuitable: Primary spot-gold benchmark, documented rolled futures strategy returns or announcement-window inference from the date label alone.
datasets.continuity: Basis/carry and contract switches can contaminate chained-close returns. Vendor metadata starts 2000-08-30; it cannot cover 1994/1999 cycle windows. COMEX settlement is not a post-14:00 ET quote.
datasets.alternatives: New licensed London gold AM/PM benchmark IDs for spot research; licensed timestamped XAU/USD or explicit single-contract futures for narrow FOMC windows. Retain gold unchanged as the legacy futures ID.

datasets.original_identifier: Board H.15 / Treasury 10-year constant maturity; FRED DGS10
datasets.producer: Federal Reserve Board / US Treasury yield-curve inputs
datasets.suitable: Nominal long-term yield conditions and basis-point changes.
datasets.unsuitable: A real yield, a bond price/total return or a timestamp-synchronous intraday control.
datasets.continuity: Constant maturity is fitted, not a held bond. Curve/input methods and holiday gaps matter.
datasets.alternatives: DFII10 real TIPS yield, DGS2 short-end expectations, and separate 10-year breakevens for decomposition.

datasets.original_identifier: ICE USDX cash index; secondary Yahoo DX-Y.NYB
datasets.suitable: A fixed developed-currency-basket dollar measure with clear ICE attribution and cleared rights.
datasets.unsuitable: The broad trade-weighted dollar, an FX pair, index futures returns or all US trading-partner exposure.
datasets.continuity: Six-currency basket, euro weight 57.6%; 1999 euro transition. Vendor firstTradeDate precedes the 1973 base/launch convention, so backcasts require proof.
datasets.alternatives: DTWEXBGS nominal broad trade-weighted dollar (2006 onward); separate historical DTWEXM/DTWEXB panels, never a silent splice.

datasets.original_identifier: NYMEX CL underlying contract; vendor Yahoo CL=F continuation
datasets.producer: NYMEX/CME contract market; vendor continuation construction not verified
datasets.suitable: Qualified signed futures-price context, with explicit roll and delivery caveats.
datasets.unsuitable: Default physical spot-oil benchmark, physical production/consumption quantities or chained strategy returns without a roll specification.
datasets.continuity: Vendor metadata starts 2000-08-23; April 2020 expiry/storage effects and legitimate negative prices defeat generic log/percentage-return assumptions.
datasets.alternatives: EIA Cushing WTI spot, FRED comparison identifier DCOILWTICO, under a new ID; add inventories/production/consumption separately. Preserve wti as futures.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUUR0000SA0; FRED CPIAUCNS
datasets.suitable: Official all-items 12-month CPI inflation, purchasing-power comparisons with caveats, and the specified NSA escalation concept.
datasets.unsuitable: Seasonally adjusted monthly momentum or an individual household's exact inflation experience.
datasets.continuity: Seasonality affects short-horizon changes; annual weight/method changes do not make the index a fixed historical basket.
datasets.alternatives: Existing cpi for SA month-on-month analysis and pce for a broader consumption-price concept; no replacement needed.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUUR0000SA0L1E; FRED CPILFENS
datasets.suitable: Official 12-month CPI excluding food and energy.
datasets.unsuitable: All household price pressure, SA monthly core momentum or a real-time surprise without the actual release vintage.
datasets.continuity: Core composition/weights change; short NSA month-to-month moves retain seasonality.
datasets.alternatives: Existing core_cpi for SA monthly momentum and core_pce for a different scope; no silent blending.

datasets.original_identifier: DOL ETA UI Weekly Claims / initial SA; FRED ICSA
datasets.producer: US Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration
datasets.suitable: Timely weekly signals of insured layoffs and labour-market deterioration.
datasets.unsuitable: The total unemployed population, all layoffs, or a complete monthly labour-market count.
datasets.continuity: Week ending Saturday is a reference period, not Thursday publication. Seasonality, holidays, backlog and state reporting can distort individual weeks.
datasets.alternatives: Initial NSA claims (ICNSA), continuing claims (CCSA) and a clearly labelled four-week average, not fabricated daily interpolation.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS JOLTS total nonfarm openings; FRED JTSJOL
datasets.producer: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
datasets.suitable: Surveyed unfilled positions at the last business day of the month and vacancy demand.
datasets.unsuitable: Payroll jobs created, monthly hires, exact online vacancy advertisements or a real-time count of all available jobs.
datasets.continuity: Stock at a reference date, not an average flow. Vacancy levels and rates answer different questions as the employment base changes.
datasets.alternatives: JTSJOR vacancy rate, JTSHIR hires and JTSQUR quits rate; preserve stock/flow definitions separately.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS LNS11300000; FRED CIVPART
datasets.suitable: Civilian labour-force participation among the noninstitutional population aged 16+.
datasets.unsuitable: Unemployment, employment/population or a pure cyclical slack measure unaffected by ageing.
datasets.continuity: Demographic composition and population controls matter; denominator scope differs from payroll employment.
datasets.alternatives: Prime-age participation (LNS11300060), prime-age employment/population and existing unemployment.

datasets.original_identifier: BLS CES0500000003; same FRED identifier
datasets.suitable: Average nominal gross hourly earnings of all private payroll employees.
datasets.unsuitable: Fixed-composition wage inflation, benefits-inclusive compensation, median earnings or real purchasing power without an explicit deflator.
datasets.continuity: Job-composition shocks can raise the average while low-paid workers lose jobs. All-employee scope differs from longer production/nonsupervisory series.
datasets.alternatives: Employment Cost Index wage/compensation measures; separately deflated real earnings and the older nonsupervisory series with its narrower scope.

datasets.original_identifier: St. Louis Fed DGS5 minus DFII5; FRED T5YIE
datasets.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculation, Treasury yield inputs
datasets.suitable: Market-based five-year inflation compensation and comparison with nominal/real yields.
datasets.unsuitable: A pure survey expectation, realized future inflation, or the real-yield variable itself.
datasets.continuity: Inflation risk and TIPS liquidity premia matter, especially under stress. Maturity and quote times must match; no pre-2003 backfill from future CPI.
datasets.alternatives: DFII5, DGS5 and a separately permissioned SPF inflation forecast at its own horizon/frequency.

datasets.original_identifier: Census Advance Monthly Retail Trade / total retail and food services; FRED RSAFS
datasets.suitable: Nominal retail/food-service spending and near-term goods-oriented demand.
datasets.unsuitable: Real sales volume, all household services consumption, material tonnage or a standalone real-consumption measure.
datasets.continuity: Seasonal/trading-day adjustment is not inflation adjustment. Industry definitions and annual benchmarks can revise history.
datasets.alternatives: Real PCE and explicit goods/services components; a correctly matched retail deflator only under a new documented derived series.

datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCERX; FRED PCEC96
datasets.producer: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.suitable: Broad inflation-adjusted household-consumption activity, including services.
datasets.unsuitable: Nominal retail sales, physical tonnes of consumption, or an additive sum of all chained-dollar components.
datasets.continuity: Verified current FRED table begins in 2007; do not advertise 1959 coverage without a separately validated source response. SAAR levels do not make monthly growth annualized.
datasets.alternatives: BEA direct account/history and real goods/services components; validate the exact monthly table/endpoint mapping before extending history.

datasets.original_identifier: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment; FRED UMCSENT
datasets.producer: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
datasets.suitable: Qualified household attitudes and sentiment, using source-release and delivery-lag information.
datasets.unsuitable: Actual spending/output, a live same-month FRED reading, or a homogeneous monthly sample back to the first 1952 observation.
datasets.continuity: Do not fill sparse early observations or interpret the April-July 2024 survey-mode change as wholly economic. Follow the specified source attribution.
datasets.alternatives: Separate expectations/current-conditions components if rights-cleared; NY Fed consumer expectations as a different concept, not a drop-in replacement.

datasets.original_identifier: Census/HUD New Residential Construction, total privately owned starts; FRED HOUST
datasets.suitable: Residential construction starts and forward demand for housing-related inputs.
datasets.unsuitable: All construction/infrastructure activity, completed dwellings, material consumption tonnage or the raw number started during the month.
datasets.continuity: Thousands at SAAR; weather, sampling error and multifamily volatility matter. Use an NSA series for literal monthly counts.
datasets.alternatives: Existing permits, single/multifamily components, completions (COMPUTSA) and construction put-in-place spending.

datasets.original_identifier: Census/HUD Building Permits Survey, total privately owned authorizations; FRED PERMIT
datasets.suitable: Authorized residential pipeline in permit-issuing places.
datasets.unsuitable: Starts/completions, all US building work, nonresidential infrastructure or tonnes of aggregate demand.
datasets.continuity: SAAR units and permit-issuing geography must be retained. An authorization does not guarantee subsequent construction.
datasets.alternatives: Existing starts; completions, nonresidential/public construction spending and Missouri/local BPS under separate regional selectors.

datasets.original_identifier: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed-rate national average; FRED MORTGAGE30US
datasets.suitable: Broad weekly mortgage financing conditions for the defined borrower/product sample.
datasets.unsuitable: Every borrower's available rate, daily policy-event response, APR or a homogeneous unchanged survey methodology across November 2022.
datasets.continuity: Rates/points/sample selection and the 2022 method break matter. Follow actual release/reference weekdays rather than manufacturing a weekly grid.
datasets.alternatives: 15-year PMMS and rate/points distributions where permitted; mortgage credit availability and lending standards as different explanatory variables.

datasets.original_identifier: Board G.17 total industrial production; FRED INDPRO
datasets.suitable: Real manufacturing/mining/utilities output-cycle context.
datasets.unsuitable: Economy-wide GDP, construction output or physical tonnes of one commodity.
datasets.continuity: Industry weights, energy/weather effects and annual benchmarks matter; an index with a 2017 base is not the same economic object as a price index.
datasets.alternatives: Manufacturing/mining/utilities components, capacity utilization (TCU) and genuinely physical commodity production/stock datasets.

datasets.original_identifier: St. Louis Fed DGS10 minus DGS2; FRED T10Y2Y
datasets.producer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculation, Treasury yield inputs
datasets.suitable: Nominal Treasury curve slope and inversion regimes.
datasets.unsuitable: A causal recession forecast, term premium alone, a bond return or a pure expected policy path.
datasets.continuity: Level is a percentage-point yield difference although source units say Percent: 1.00 equals 100 bp. Negative values are valid; missing legs cannot be filled silently.
datasets.alternatives: DGS10 and DGS2 inputs; a separately defined 10-year/3-month slope and reviewed term-premium estimates.

datasets.original_identifier: ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS; FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2
datasets.suitable: Licensed recent speculative-grade credit-risk/financial-conditions context.
datasets.unsuitable: Default probability, corporate financing cost for every issuer, a bond total return or a free full-history 2008-cycle study.
datasets.continuity: Current three-year FRED window, model/constituent changes and stale/illiquid bond marks limit interpretation. Levels are quoted percent spreads; changes should be bp/pp.
datasets.alternatives: Licensed original ICE history; a distinct reviewed corporate-minus-Treasury spread or published financial-conditions index, never falsely called the same OAS.

datasets.original_identifier: ICE BofA US Corporate Index OAS; FRED BAMLC0A0CM
datasets.suitable: Licensed recent investment-grade credit conditions, distinguished from high yield.
datasets.unsuitable: A default probability, total return, exact funding rate or unrestricted long-history cycle comparator.
datasets.continuity: Rolling three-year FRED access and changing index constituents/models; Treasury-curve-relative option adjustment is not the same as a simple yield spread.
datasets.alternatives: Licensed original ICE history; distinct matched-maturity corporate/Treasury measures with their own IDs and permissions.
